title: unify-session-contracts-and-retry-profiles-tri-sdk-release
author: Leah Ortiz
description: Motivation: current SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) expose subtly different session and retry ergonomics which complicate cross-team integrations and produces intermittent production bugs around token refresh and streaming cancellation. This PR consolidates the session abstraction, harmonizes retry profile names and defaults, and applies lightweight API surface alignment across the three official SDKs so downstream services can rely on a single mental model. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce SessionHandle interface (stable) implemented in each SDK with consistent methods: acquire(), renewLease(), close(), onBackoff(callback). 2) Standardize retry preset names (fast, balanced, conservative) and map legacy profiles to new names in a compat shim. 3) Streaming helpers: add cancelable async iterator wrappers and a nullable resume-token metadata field to unify resume semantics. 4) Token refresh: centralize delegated-credential hooks and provide a single credential callback signature for all SDKs. 5) Tests: add cross-sdk integration matrix in CI that validates token rotation and streaming cancel/resume in three environments. 6) Docs and changelogs for tri-sdk bump. Compatibility and rollout: this is a non-breaking ergonomics improvement; all legacy names are supported via a compatibility layer that emits a deprecation warning for one release cycle. Consumers that directly relied on private internals will need small refactors (see migration notes). Checklist: - [x] design doc: ENG-2309 linked - [x] unit & integration tests - [x] TS/Python/Go example apps updated - [x] changelog entries for each SDK - [x] staged release plan (canary then general rollout). High level commit summary and changed areas included below. CI: full matrix passed after flaky ts-streaming test was retried once. Merge: squash and merge; commit message includes migration notes and cross-sdk version bumps.

Backward-compatible shim maps legacy retry names and emits deprecation warnings for one release. Canaries available for testing.
